problems.location: Learning objectives
problems.lesson_text: Design diagnostic assessment frameworks and motivation-supportive interventions using evidence-centered design and construct learning progressions to systematically mitigate misconceptions and identity threat.
problems.source_text:
Evaluate an AI product, policy, or process against the science of learning and development, and tell whether it builds a capacity or replaces it, by age and stage

problems.lesson_text: Is the program treating the learner as an isolated consumer of algorithmic micro-content (deficit model)
problems.source_text: This idea has sometimes been associated with a “deficit” model of cultural difference, in which consideration of cultural differences among students is conceived as a way to compensate for academic disadvantages that some groups may share.
problems.reason: In the source the deficit model means treating learners' cultural differences as disadvantages to make up for, not consuming algorithmic micro-content, so the lesson misdefines the term.

problems.location: Exercise 2.1: Diagnosing flaws in study regimens that conflate fluent re-reading with reconstructive retrieval and spaced practice / block 4

problems.source_text: The results suggest that actively retrieving the material soon after studying it is more productive than spending the same amount of time repeatedly reading.
problems.reason: The grading key treats answering questions right after reading as a flaw with little benefit, while the source presents retrieval soon after study as productive.

problems.location: Concept 5: Learning Technologies and AI Affordances: Cognitive Alignment and Ecosystem Integration / block 1
